evidence.computation: Exact or certified enclosed growth quantities with explicit interest-versus-balance target; interest is selected before final rounding. Monthly payment and deposit schedules contain exactly twelve times the stated years in whole periods. Existing annuity and two-phase equations remain available. Equal monthly cashflows include an explicit opening balance and start/end deposit timing. The closed form equals a separately defined monthly recurrence; interest excludes all contributions.
assumptions: Equal deposits occur at the specified start or end of each month, defaulting to end when absent. The term is a nonnegative whole number of months; rate is nominal annual with monthly compounding.
Annual rates are nominal fractions; compounding frequency is explicit or uses the documented default.
Two-phase growth, when supported, has no intervening deposits or withdrawals.
Lump-sum growth uses nonnegative principal and duration and a positive periodic growth factor; monthly cashflow amounts are nonnegative.
untrusted: English recognition and decimal-to-request conversion; mathematical proof does not establish that the sentence was read correctly.

evidence.computation: Exact rational economics arithmetic. Real GDP satisfies C*D=N*100. The default real interest rate preserves nominal purchasing power: (1+real)*(1+inflation)=1+nominal; the subtraction approximation is selected only when explicit.
assumptions: The deflator is a positive index with base 100.
Amounts retain the scale named in the question.
Gross output and population counts are nonnegative; source and destination CPI indices are positive. CPI conversion may preserve a signed money amount, such as a debt.
untrusted: English recognition, unit-scale selection, and numeric parsing.

evidence.computation: Apply discounts in sequence, tax the explicitly selected original or discounted price, and answer final price, tax amount, or savings against full price including tax. Inventory duration and turnover retain distinct observed and requested time periods; reorder points convert demand and lead time to the same typed time unit in the kernel.
assumptions: Each discount is from 0% to 100%; the price and tax rate are nonnegative.
Tax applies after discounts unless the original-price tax base is explicitly requested; savings compares the paid total with full price including tax.
Inventory days uses average inventory/COGS times the observation period. Absent an explicit period, the inherited annual model uses 365 days.
Demand is constant over lead time. A model year is exactly 365 days; calendar months, business days and changing demand need additional information.
untrusted: English recognition, classification of each percentage, and numeric parsing.
